title: Introduce cooperative microbatching shim and opt-in KV compaction oracle
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: tail-latency regressions under mixed traffic (short chat turns + long streaming calls) have been traced to contention between the ingress admission path and the continuous batcher, and to KV cache churn from eager eviction heuristics. This ticket introduces a small, cooperative microbatching shim that sits between ingress and the batcher to shape request bursts and provide prefetch hints, plus an opt-in asynchronous 'KV compaction oracle' that consolidates cold keys and signals the scheduler to reclaim leases without blocking the hotpath. Goals: reduce tail P95/P99 by 20–30% for 99th-percentile workloads, lower CPU overhead of prefetching by avoiding redundant work, and provide safe rollout controls (feature flag + per-tenant gate).
acceptance_criteria: New microbatching shim deployed behind feature flag that can be enabled per-tenant
P95 and P99 token latency improvement >= 15% in synthetic mixed workload compared to baseline
KV compaction oracle reduces kvcache high-water churn metric by >= 30% in stress runs
No regression in correctness: model outputs identical (or within tolerance) for pinned sessions
End-to-end tests for lease reclaim flow and race conditions added to CI
Performance dashboards and alerts instrumented (per-route latency, prefetch hit-rate, oracle compactions)
steps: Design review with runtime and storage teams: finalize contracts for prefetch_hint and compact_hint signals
Prototype shim as a small Rust crate that implements an adaptive latency budget and token-count coalescer
Implement KV compaction oracle as background actor with rate limiter and snapshot-safe compaction plan
Add feature flag and per-tenant config in control plane; expose knobs in Console (prefetch window, oracle aggressiveness)
Bench locally and in perf-N cluster; capture flamegraphs and telemetry for iteration
Create PRs, request security review (KMS/key handling is unaffected but audit required), and merge
Canary rollout against 5% of traffic, monitor for regressions, then ramp to 50% and 100%
Post-rollout: run a 48h soak with mixed production traffic and finalize docs/observability runbook

comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Triage notes — paired profiling with infra and noticed periodic CPU spikes correlated with bulk prefetches from ingress. Proposed microbatch shim to smooth bursts and attach prefetch hints so KV layer can avoid redundant loads.

2026-02-18 Tomás Rivera: Design meeting summary — runtime + storage agreed on a minimal contract: shim emits prefetch_hint(key_prefix, expected_tokens, priority) and oracle accepts compact_hint(shard, epoch, candidate_keys). Decided oracle will never evict hot keys; it only reconciles 'stale-slot' candidates produced by sampler.

2026-02-25 Eng review: Prototype implemented. Early perf runs in perf-N show P99 down 18% on mixed 60/40 short/long workload, but CPU increased ~6% due to background oracle compaction; exploring batching compaction operations to amortize cost.

2026-03-03 Security: Requested review for background actor because it touches shard metadata. Security asked for stricter audit logs for compaction actions and a KMS-backed signing of compaction plans. Added to scope.

2026-03-07 QA: Added integration tests for lease reclaim race where a session that was compacted is rehydrated; verified fallbacks preserve correctness. Found a race where the shim could over-coalesce low-priority streaming requests; mitigated by lowering coalescing window for function-call routes.

2026-03-11 Tomás Rivera: PRs opened (runtime/#11890, kvcache/#447). Blocker: the infra image needs liburing support to run the compaction IO path efficiently. Filed infra ticket and coordinated image bump with platform team.

2026-03-12 Aisha Kapoor: Updated rollout plan — start with internal customers only (dedicated accounts), enable feature flag per-tenant with a conservative oracle aggressiveness default. Monitor oracle_compactions_per_min and prefetch_hit_rate in the first 24h.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive compaction reduces memory but increases IO and CPU; therefore default oracle policy is conservative and tunable. We intentionally keep shim out of critical fast path — it only suggests microbatches and prefetch hints; batcher still enforces final admission. This minimizes blast radius.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in microbatching shim and an asynchronous KV compaction actor behind feature flags. Initial rollout to internal tenants only; console exposes configuration and basic telemetry.
observability_changes: New metrics: shim.coalesce_window_ms, shim.coalesced_requests, prefetch_hint_rate, oracle.compactions_started, oracle.compactions_completed, kvcache.churn_high_water
follow_up_tasks: Add adaptive knob that ties oracle aggressiveness to cluster load
Evaluate migrating oracle IO path to io_uring where supported (follow ENG-420420 for infra image upgrade)
Consider exposing per-route policies in Console for fine-grained control
